issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex lacks case-insensitive flag while HAS_KEYWORD has it
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, HAS_KEYWORD uses the /i flag but HAS_PERCENTAGE does not. Percentage selectors don't have case issues, but the asymmetry suggests the data was not examined carefully. Worth a comment explaining why, or normalizing both. Small thing, but the flags ARE the data shape here.

issues.description: import-notation 'url' branch returns when url() IS present, inverting the gate
issues.detail: Look at the data: if primary is 'url' and params already contain url(), we skip the check entirely. That means a malformed or mixed url()/string param goes unvalidated. The named-where-possible style in font-weight gates on the opposite token; this one gates on its own preferred token. Verify this matches actual rule semantics before merging.

issues.description: selectorRegex /./ sentinel is clever where undefined would compose
issues.detail: Building a regex that matches everything just to satisfy walkRules' filter signature is the kind of cleverness rule 4 warns about. If walkRules accepts an absent filter, branch on that. If not, the /./ is fine but deserves a one-line comment. Data structure choice: the filter is sometimes-present; encode that directly.

issues.description: Pre-filter regexes duplicate parser knowledge that may drift
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED, HAS_NUMERIC, HAS_PERCENTAGE, HAS_KEYWORD all encode a subset of what valueParser/parseSelector will later prove. If the keyword sets change, the regex and the parser-side check must stay in sync. The constants are derived from the same source sets, which is the right call. Add a comment naming this dependency so future edits don't drift.

issues.description: media-feature-range context regex /(?:min|max)-/i can false-positive in values
issues.detail: The pre-filter scans entire params for min-/max- which could appear inside a calc() or value context unrelated to a feature name. False positives only cost a parser pass (correctness preserved), so this is fine — but worth a one-line note that the regex is a fast over-approximation, not a semantic check.

issues.description: No measurement evidence cited for the perf win
issues.detail: Rule 2: measure. The PR description says 'performance' but doesn't show a before/after number on a realistic stylesheet. The changes look reasonable as fast-path early-outs, but the discipline is to record the win (even rough microseconds per 10k decls) so future refactors know what budget they're protecting. Cheap to add to the changeset or PR body.

review.summary: The diff is the right shape: pre-compute a regex from the same data that drives the rule, use it as a cheap gate before the expensive parser pass. Data dominates, and here the data is "does this value/selector contain a token the rule could possibly care about." That's a good filter. Two concrete concerns: the import-notation 'url' branch inverts the gating direction relative to the others and may be a semantic bug worth double-checking, and the keyframe-selector regex pair has an inconsistent case-insensitive flag. The /./ sentinel and lack of measured numbers in the changeset are minor taste issues. Overall SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE with one suspect line.
